name: scummvm
why: Runs a huge back catalogue of classic adventure games, an old-school environment worth an evening.

brief.what_it_is: ScummVM is a program that runs classic graphical adventure and role-playing games. You supply the original game data files, and it replaces the games' original executables so they run on modern systems. The homepage says it is a complete rewrite of those executables rather than an emulator. It lists over 325 supported adventure games from studios such as LucasArts, Sierra On-Line, Revolution Software, Cyan and Westwood, and runs on many platforms, including Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, Switch and Dreamcast.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to play classic adventure games on systems they were never designed for, and it presents the project as a preservation and playability effort that accepts code contributions and donations.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not describe the internals in detail. It says ScummVM replaces each game's shipped executable and needs the original data files to be present. The news posts describe a per-game engine model: each game family has an engine, and games are added or fixed engine by engine.
brief.install_notes: You need the original game data files. The homepage says you can use your old floppies or get a free copy of The Colony from ZOOM Platform. For the testing builds in the news, the steps are to grab a recent daily development build, add your game directory to ScummVM, and play. Harvester needs a supported version, and the ScummVM wiki covers extracting its data files. The Colony and Dungeon Master are in testing and need builds from the daily development channel rather than the stable release.
brief.standout: It is a rewrite of the games' engines rather than an emulator, which is why it can run so many titles natively on so many platforms. The release is also notable for its scale: the 2026.4.0 post says it added 194 newly supported games and 12 new engines.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage news runs from Oct 2, 2026 to Oct 15, 2026, with a stable release 2026.4.0 "Never-slop" dated Oct 11, 2026, and new public-testing announcements for The Colony, Dungeon Master and Lord Avalot d'Argent. The post on the 2026.4.0 release says the team follows a new release cadence.
brief.caveats: You must already own or legally obtain the original game data files; ScummVM does not ship them. Some titles are only in testing and require daily development builds. The homepage does not state the license. Platform support varies by port, and the 2026.4.0 post says some ports lag the main release. The compatibility page lists how well each game works, and I did not open it.
quotes: ScummVM is a program which allows you to run certain classic graphical adventure and role-playing games, provided you already have their data files.
ScummVM is a complete rewrite of these games' executables and is not an emulator.
The clever part about this: ScummVM just replaces the executables shipped with the games, allowing you to play them on systems for which they were never designed!
